findings.title: The same-parent check treats unrelated sites under a public suffix as the instance's own domain.
findings.body: For hosts with the same number of labels (more than two), the code compares everything after the first label. So `foo.co.uk` against an instance at `forum.co.uk`, or `someone.github.io` against `forum.github.io`, counts as the same domain, and the full URL path is shown for an unrelated site. To fix this, compare against the registrable domain (public-suffix aware), or limit the match to `website_host` equal to the instance host or one of its parent domains.

findings.title: `include_website_name` lacks the `?`, so the serializer never calls it.
findings.body: ActiveModel::Serializers only checks `include_<attr>?` methods. Without the `?`, this method is never called, so `website_name` is always serialized, as `null` when there is no website. Rename it to `include_website_name?`.

held.title: The website label now comes from a static server field and can go stale after the website is edited.
held.body: The old `websiteName` was a computed property on the website value, so it updated whenever `model.website` changed. `model.website_name` is set only when the server serializes the user. If a user changes their website in preferences and the same client-side user model is reused without a reload, the link points to the new `website` URL while its text still shows the old name, or is hidden if the website was empty before. I could not check whether the profile route always reloads the model. If it does not, refresh `website_name` from the save response or compute it on the client.
